source: FAO/OIE/World Bank, "Good Practices for Biosecurity in the Pig Sector - Issues and Options in Developing and Transition Countries", FAO Animal Production and Health Paper No. 169, Rome, 2010.
text: Biosecurity in pig production rests on three steps, in order of effectiveness: (1) Segregation - creating and maintaining barriers so infected animals or contaminated materials cannot reach uninfected pigs; this is the single most effective step, since if a pathogen never enters a holding, no infection can occur. (2) Cleaning - thoroughly removing visible dirt, manure and organic material from anything (vehicles, equipment, footwear) that must cross the barrier, since most pathogen contamination is carried in faecal material, urine or secretions on surfaces. (3) Disinfection - applied only after thorough cleaning, since disinfectants cannot penetrate visible dirt and are often unavailable or misused under village conditions; it should be treated as a final 'polishing' step, not a substitute for cleaning.
